issues.legal_issue: A plaint amendment sought after trial has commenced may be allowed where the matter could not have been raised earlier despite due diligence and the amendment assists determination of the real controversy without changing the suit’s character or prejudicing the opposing party.
material_facts: The appellants brought a civil suit to set aside an earlier ex parte decree, and the record of the suit in which that decree had been made was untraceable.
After issues were framed and two official witnesses had been examined, the appellants sought to amend the plaint to add particulars of the land and related allegations.
The court considered that the missing record could have prevented the appellants from obtaining correct particulars earlier.
The proposed amendment did not change the character or nature of the suit and introduced no fresh ground.
The amendment would not prejudice the defendants, and the trial had progressed only to the examination of two official witnesses.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the application to amend the plaint was accepted, and the trial court was directed to proceed on the amended plaint.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, an amendment sought after commencement of trial requires the court to be satisfied that despite due diligence the party could not have raised the matter earlier. Amendments necessary to determine the real question in controversy should generally be allowed where they cause no injustice or prejudice. The Court relied on Abdul Rehman v. Mohd. Ruldu, J. Samuel v. Gattu Mahesh, and Rameshkumar Agarwal v. Rajmala Exports (P) Ltd.

rule.if: civil_plaint_amendment and trial_commenced and earlier_details_unavailable_despite_diligence and amendment_preserves_suit_character and amendment_adds_no_fresh_ground and no_opponent_prejudice and trial_at_early_stage

predicates.civil_plaint_amendment: A party in a civil suit sought to amend the plaint.
predicates.trial_commenced: The court had begun the trial before the amendment application was made.
predicates.earlier_details_unavailable_despite_dili: The party could not obtain or raise the relevant matter before trial began despite diligence.
predicates.amendment_preserves_suit_character: The proposed amendment leaves the character and nature of the suit unchanged.
predicates.amendment_adds_no_fresh_ground: The proposed amendment does not introduce a fresh ground of claim.
predicates.no_opponent_prejudice: The proposed amendment would not prejudice the opposing party.
predicates.trial_at_early_stage: Only a limited portion of the trial had taken place when amendment was sought.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to amend a civil plaint after trial has begun, the amendment is permitted if the matter could not have been raised earlier despite diligence, the amendment preserves the suit’s character, adds no fresh ground, causes no prejudice, and the trial remains at an early stage.
